svg.aria-label: Chart comparing the growth of O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n) and O(n squared)
svg.title: Chart comparing the growth of O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n) and O(n squared)
svg.text: Five growth rates on one pair of axes; the exponential is marked where it leaves the scale

text.tspan: the same axes for every curve: how many operations as the input grows. Where a curve leaves the box, that algorithm has left

g.text: O(2^n) is vertical by n=7 and O(n^2) is gone by n=10 - both are unusable at any real scale
the gap between O(n) and O(n log n) is small; the gap between O(n log n) and O(n^2) is the whole chart
constants are invisible here on purpose: a 'slow' O(n) beats a 'fast' O(n^2) once n is large enough
